question: Can every positive target supply a displaced second query observation when a nearly complete active view is allowed to touch the image edge while exact foreign targets remain absent?

predecessor.single_change: Reduce only the active-query image-margin floor from 32px to 0px. Retain 0.98 target completeness, depth visibility, maximum-baseline ranking, 0.05-1.10m reachability and zero projected foreign-target vertices. Geometry diagnosis found DR01 frame 248 at 0.969m with 0.993 target completeness and 0.387px margin.

selection.ranking: Maximum available at-least-98%-inside baseline up to 1.10m, then minimum frame gap, maximum depth-visible ratio, visible vertices and projected area, then earliest frame; same-scene negative frames additionally require zero projected vertices from the exact foreign target.

forbidden_after_freeze: open candidate RGB or call a model before all active query frames are fixed
relax the 0.98 target completeness, depth visibility, exact-target absence or ranking after observing selected RGB
replace an active frame after downstream failure
use provider geometry or target identity in a runtime binding decision
claim provider-selected recorded views prove a user can execute the observation action
claim_boundary: This zero-model source successor admits a nearly complete target at the image edge and uses privileged 3RScan pose, depth and registered instance geometry to freeze recorded active query views for three consumed targets while preserving two exact-target-absent sibling-door negatives. It measures source reachability only; it is not runtime binding, arbitrary sibling rejection, provider-independent generalization, user-action feasibility, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, Android deployment, benefit, reliability or safety evidence.
